title.raw: 卷三十五 志第二十五 州郡一 Volume 35 Treatises 25: Administrative Districts 1

sentences.zh: 志第二十五 州郡一

translations.literal: Treatise 25: Administrative Districts 1
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 25: Administrative Districts, Part 1

sentences.zh: ○揚州南徐州徐州南兗州兗州

translations.literal: ○ Yang Province, Southern Xu Province, Xu Province, Southern Yan Province, Yan Province
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yang, Southern Xu, Xu, Southern Yan, and Yan Provinces

sentences.zh: 唐堯之世，置十有二牧，及禹平水土，更制九州，冀州堯都，土界廣遠，濟、河為兗州，海、岱為青州，海、岱及淮為徐州，淮、海為揚州，荊及衡陽為荊州，荊、河為豫州，華陽、黑水為梁州，黑水、西河為雍州。

translations.literal: In the era of Tang Yao, twelve supervisors were established. When Yu pacified the waters and earth, he reorganized the Nine Provinces. Jizhou was Yao's capital; its territory was broad and far-reaching. The Ji and Yellow rivers formed Yan Province; the sea and Mount Tai formed Qing Province; the sea, Mount Tai, and the Huai formed Xu Province; the Huai and sea formed Yang Province; Jing and Mount Hengyang formed Jing Province; Jing and the Yellow River formed Yu Province; Mount Huayang and the Black Water formed Liang Province; the Black Water and the Western River formed Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yao of Tang, twelve regional overseers were appointed. After Yu brought the floods under control and settled the land, he reorganized the realm into nine provinces. Jizhou, where Yao had his capital, encompassed a vast extent of territory. Yan was defined by the Ji and Yellow rivers; Qing by the sea and Mount Tai; Xu by the sea, Mount Tai, and the Huai; Yang by the Huai and the sea; Jing by the Jing region and Mount Hengyang; Yu by the Jing region and the Yellow River; Liang by Mount Huayang and the Black Water; and Yong by the Black Water and the Western River.

sentences.zh: 自虞至殷，無所改變。

translations.literal: From the era of Yu of Xia down to the Yin dynasty, nothing was changed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xia through the Shang, the arrangement remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 周氏既有天下，以徐並青，以梁並雍，分冀州之地以為幽、並。

translations.literal: When the Zhou possessed the realm, they merged Xu into Qing, merged Liang into Yong, and divided the territory of Jizhou to form You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Zhou held the empire, they annexed Xu to Qing and Liang to Yong, and carved out You and Bing from the lands of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 漢初又立徐、梁二州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Xu and Liang provinces were again established.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Han, Xu and Liang were re-established as separate provinces.

sentences.zh: 武帝攘卻胡、越，開地斥境，南置交趾，北置朔方，改雍曰涼，改梁曰益，凡為十三州，而司隸部三輔、三河諸郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu repelled the Hu and Yue, opened territory and extended the borders, established Jiaozhi in the south and Shuofang in the north, changed Yong to Liang and Liang to Yi, making thirteen provinces in all, while the Directorate of the Minister of Works governed the Three Metropolitan Areas and the Three He commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu drove back the northern and southern barbarians, expanded the frontiers, set up Jiaozhi in the south and Shuofang in the north, renamed Yong as Liang and Liang as Yi, and thus made thirteen provinces in all, with the metropolitan Directorate of the Minister of Works overseeing the Three Metropolitan Areas and the Three He commanderies.

sentences.zh: 東京無複朔方，改交趾曰交州，凡十二州；

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital no longer had Shuofang; Jiaozhi was changed to Jiao Province, making twelve provinces in all;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Eastern Han, Shuofang was abolished and Jiaozhi was renamed Jiao Province, leaving twelve provinces in all;

sentences.zh: 司隸所部如故。

translations.literal: the territory under the Directorate of the Minister of Works remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: while the metropolitan Directorate's jurisdiction stayed as before.

sentences.zh: 及三國鼎歭，吳得揚、荊、交三州，蜀得益州，魏氏猶得九焉。

translations.literal: When the Three Kingdoms stood in tripartite balance, Wu obtained the three provinces of Yang, Jing, and Jiao; Shu obtained Yi Province; and Wei still held nine.
translations.idiomatic: When the three kingdoms divided the realm, Wu held Yang, Jing, and Jiao; Shu held Yi; and Wei retained nine provinces.

sentences.zh: 吳又分交為廣。

translations.literal: Wu further divided Jiao to form Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu later split Jiao to create Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 魏末平蜀，又分益為梁。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei, when Shu was pacified, Yi was further divided to form Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei conquered Shu at the end of the period, Yi was further divided to form Liang.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年，天下一統，凡十有六州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, the realm was unified, making sixteen provinces in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taikang (280), when Emperor Wu of Jin reunified the empire, there were sixteen provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 後又分涼、雍為秦，分荊、揚為江，分益為寧，分幽為平，而為二十矣。

translations.literal: Later Liang and Yong were divided to form Qin; Jing and Yang were divided to form Jiang; Yi was divided to form Ning; You was divided to form Ping, making twenty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Qin was split from Liang and Yong, Jiang from Jing and Yang, Ning from Yi, and Ping from You, bringing the total to twenty.

sentences.zh: 自夷狄亂華，司、冀、雍、涼、青、並、兗、豫、幽、平諸州一時淪沒，遺民南渡，並僑置牧司，非舊土也。

translations.literal: Since the barbarians threw China into disorder, the provinces of Si, Ji, Yong, Liang, Qing, Bing, Yan, Yu, You, and Ping were all lost at once. The surviving populace crossed south, and supervisory offices were all established as frontier administrations—not on the old territory.
translations.idiomatic: After the northern peoples threw the Central Plains into chaos, Si, Ji, Yong, Liang, Qing, Bing, Yan, Yu, You, and Ping were overrun in a single stroke. Refugees fled south, and provincial administrations were set up as exclave jurisdictions far from their original territories.

sentences.zh: 江左又分荊為湘，或離或合，凡有揚、荊、湘、江、梁、益、交、廣，其徐州則有過半，豫州唯得譙城而已。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi they further divided Jing to form Xiang; some were separated and some reunited. In all there were Yang, Jing, Xiang, Jiang, Liang, Yi, Jiao, and Guang; of Xu Province they held more than half; of Yu Province they held only Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi, Jing was further split to form Xiang, with boundaries shifting repeatedly. The realm held Yang, Jing, Xiang, Jiang, Liang, Yi, Jiao, and Guang; of Xu, somewhat more than half; of Yu, only the city of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 及至宋世，分揚州為南徐，徐州為南兗，揚州之江西悉屬豫州；

translations.literal: By the Song era, Yang was divided to form Southern Xu, Xu was divided to form Southern Yan, and all the territory west of the Yangzi in Yang Province was placed under Yu Province;
translations.idiomatic: By the Liu Song period, Southern Xu was carved from Yang, Southern Yan from Xu, and all lands west of the Yangzi that had belonged to Yang were transferred to Yu;

sentences.zh: 分荊為雍，分荊、湘為郢，分荊為司，分廣為越，分青為冀，分梁為南北秦。

translations.literal: Jing was divided to form Yong; Jing and Xiang were divided to form Ying; Jing was divided to form Si; Guang was divided to form Yue; Qing was divided to form Ji; Liang was divided into Northern and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was split from Jing, Ying from Jing and Xiang, Si from Jing, Yue from Guang, Ji from Qing, and Northern and Southern Qin from Liang.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，索虜南侵，青、冀、徐、兗及豫州淮西，並皆不守；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Taizong's reign, the northern barbarians invaded south; Qing, Ji, Xu, Yan, and the Huai west of Yu Province were all abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the Northern Wei drove south; Qing, Ji, Xu, Yan, and the lands west of the Huai in Yu were all lost;

sentences.zh: 自淮以北，化成虜庭。

translations.literal: north of the Huai became barbarian territory.
translations.idiomatic: and everything north of the Huai became enemy-held land.

sentences.zh: 於是于鐘離置徐州，淮陰為北兗，而青、冀二州治贛榆之縣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xu Province was established at Zhongli, Huaiyin served as Northern Yan, and the two provinces of Qing and Ji had their seats at the county of Ganyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was then re-established at Zhongli, Huaiyin served as Northern Yan, and Qing and Ji were administered from the county of Ganyu.

sentences.zh: 今志大較以大明八年為正，其後分派，隨事記列。

translations.literal: This gazetteer takes the eighth year of Daming as its general standard; later divisions and assignments are recorded as events occur.
translations.idiomatic: This treatise generally takes the eighth year of Daming (464) as its baseline; subsequent changes are noted as they arose.

sentences.zh: 內史、侯、相，則以升明末為定焉。

translations.literal: For interior prefectures, marquisates, and chancelleries, the end of the Shengming era is taken as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: For metropolitan prefectures, marquisates, and princely chancelleries, the standard is the end of the Shengming era (477).

sentences.zh: 地理參差，其詳難舉，實由名號驟易，境土屢分，或一郡一縣，割成四五；

translations.literal: Geography is uneven; the full detail is hard to set forth, truly because names and titles change abruptly and territories are repeatedly divided—a single commandery or county may be carved into four or five parts;
translations.idiomatic: The geography is too irregular to recount in full detail, chiefly because names changed abruptly and boundaries were redrawn again and again—a single commandery or county might be split into four or five parts;

sentences.zh: 四五之中，亟有離合，千回百改，巧曆不算，尋校推求，未易精悉。

translations.literal: among those four or five parts there are frequent separations and reunions; a thousand reversals and a hundred changes—even a skilled reckoner cannot calculate them; searching and comparing by deduction, it is not easy to master precisely.
translations.idiomatic: and those fragments in turn were repeatedly merged and split. After countless changes, even the most skilled calculator could not track them all; cross-checking the sources does not yield perfect certainty.

sentences.zh: 今以班固馬彪二志、太康元康定戶、王隱《地道》、晉世《起居》、《永初郡國》、何徐《州郡》及地理雜書，互相考覆。

translations.literal: Now the two treatises of Ban Gu and Ma Biao, the household registers of Taikang and Yuankang, Wang Yin's Topography of the Land, the Jin-era Court Diaries, the Yongchu Commanderies and States, He and Xu's Provinces and Commanderies, and miscellaneous geographical books are mutually collated and checked.
translations.idiomatic: The present account cross-checks Ban Gu's and Ma Biao's treatises, the Taikang and Yuankang household registers, Wang Yin's Topography of the Land, the Jin court diaries, the Yongchu Commanderies and States, He and Xu's work on provinces and commanderies, and various other geographical compilations.

sentences.zh: 且三國無志，事出帝紀，雖立郡時見，而置縣不書。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Three Kingdoms period has no treatise; matters come from imperial annals. Although the establishment of commanderies appears at times, the establishment of counties is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, no geographical treatise survives for the Three Kingdoms period; what is known comes from imperial annals. Commandery foundations are sometimes noted, but county foundations are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 今唯以《續漢郡國》校《太康地志》，參伍異同，用相征驗。

translations.literal: Now only the Continuation of Han Commanderies and States is checked against the Taikang Gazetteer of the Land; discrepancies are compared and used for mutual verification.
translations.idiomatic: Here the Continuation of Han Commanderies and States is checked against the Taikang Gazetteer of the Land, and discrepancies between them are weighed against each other for verification.

sentences.zh: 自漢至宋，郡縣無移改者，則注雲「漢舊」，其有回徙，隨源甄別。

translations.literal: From Han to Song, where commanderies and counties underwent no relocation or change, the note reads "Han old." Where there were removals and transfers, they are distinguished according to their origin.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies and counties unchanged since Han are marked "Han old"; those that were moved or renamed are traced to their origins.

sentences.zh: 若唯雲「某無」者，則此前皆有也。

translations.literal: If it only says "such-and-such absent," then it existed before.
translations.idiomatic: When an entry simply says that a given work "does not mention" a place, that place existed in earlier sources.

sentences.zh: 若不注置立，史闕也。

translations.literal: If the date of establishment is not noted, the historical record is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: When no date of establishment is given, the historical record is silent on the point.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史，前漢刺史未有所治它州同，後漢治曆陽，魏、晉治壽春，晉平吳治建業。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yang Province: in Former Han the inspector had no fixed seat, the same as other provinces; in Later Han the seat was at Liyang; in Wei and Jin at Shouchun; after Jin pacified Wu, at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yang Province: under Former Han the inspector had no fixed seat, as with other provinces; under Later Han the seat was at Liyang; under Wei and Jin at Shouchun; after Jin conquered Wu, at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸康四年，僑立魏郡別見，肥鄉別見、元城漢舊縣，晉屬陽平二縣，後省元城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, a frontier Wei Commandery was established (see elsewhere); Feixiang (see elsewhere) and Yuancheng, an old Han county belonging to Yangping, were two counties; later Yuancheng was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiankang (338), a frontier Wei Commandery was established (see elsewhere), along with Feixiang (see elsewhere) and Yuancheng, a Han-era county that under Jin belonged to Yangping; Yuancheng was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 又僑立廣川郡別見，領廣川一縣，宋初省為縣，隸魏郡。

translations.literal: A frontier Guangchuan Commandery was also established (see elsewhere), governing one county of Guangchuan; at the beginning of Song it was reduced to a county and placed under Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A frontier Guangchuan Commandery was also set up (see elsewhere), governing only the county of Guangchuan; early in the Song it was reduced to a county subordinate to Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 江左又立高陽別見、堂邑二郡別見，高陽領北新城別見、博陸博陸縣，霍光所封，而二漢無，晉屬高陽。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi they further established frontier Gaoyang Commandery (see elsewhere) and Tangyi Commandery (see elsewhere). Gaoyang governed Beixin (see elsewhere) and Bolu. Bolu County was the fief of Huo Guang, but did not exist in the two Han dynasties; under Jin it belonged to Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi, frontier Gaoyang Commandery (see elsewhere) and Tangyi Commandery (see elsewhere) were also established. Gaoyang governed Beixin (see elsewhere) and Bolu. Bolu was the fief granted to Huo Guang and did not exist in either Han dynasty; under Jin it belonged to Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 二縣。

translations.literal: Two counties.
translations.idiomatic: These were its two counties.

sentences.zh: 堂邑，領堂邑一縣，後省堂邑並高陽，又省高陽並魏郡，並隸揚州，寄治京邑。

translations.literal: Tangyi governed one county of Tangyi; later Tangyi was abolished and merged into Gaoyang, and Gaoyang was again abolished and merged into Wei Commandery; all were placed under Yang Province with administration at the capital by attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Tangyi governed only the county of Tangyi; later Tangyi was abolished and merged into Gaoyang, and Gaoyang in turn was merged into Wei Commandery. All were subordinated to Yang Province and administered from the capital as attached jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉十一年省，以其民並建康。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen it was abolished, and its population was merged into Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia (434) it was abolished and its population incorporated into Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，分揚州之會稽、東陽、新安、永嘉、臨海五郡為東揚州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai in Yang Province were divided off to form Eastern Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaojian (454), Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai were split from Yang to form Eastern Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 大明三年罷州，以其地為王畿，以南台侍御史部諸郡，如從事之部傳焉，而東揚州直雲揚州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming the province was abolished; its territory became the royal domain. The attendant censor of the Southern Terrace oversaw the commanderies, as in the transmission of the staff of the inspector, while Eastern Yang Province was simply called Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming (459) the province was abolished and its territory made the royal domain, with a Southern Terrace attendant censor supervising its commanderies in the manner of a provincial staff. Eastern Yang was meanwhile renamed simply Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 八年，罷王畿，複立揚州，揚州還為東揚州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the royal domain was abolished, Yang Province was re-established, and Yang Province reverted to being Eastern Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (464) the royal domain was abolished, Yang was re-established, and what had been Yang reverted to Eastern Yang.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝永光元年，省東揚州並揚州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongguang under the Deposed Former Emperor, Eastern Yang Province was abolished and merged into Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongguang (465), under the Deposed Former Emperor, Eastern Yang was abolished and merged into Yang.

sentences.zh: 順帝升明三年，改揚州刺史曰牧。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, the Inspector of Yang Province was changed to Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shengming (479), under Emperor Shun, the inspector of Yang was redesignated governor.

sentences.zh: 領郡十，領縣八十。

translations.literal: It governed ten commanderies and eighty counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed ten commanderies and eighty counties.

sentences.zh: 戶一十四萬三千二百九十六，口一百四十五萬五千六百八十五。

translations.literal: Households: 143,296; persons: 1,455,685.
translations.idiomatic: Registered households: 143,296; population: 1,455,685.

sentences.zh: 丹楊令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Danyang: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Danyang: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 句容令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Jurong: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Jurong: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守，秦立，治吳。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Kuaiji: established under Qin, seat at Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Kuaiji: established under Qin, with its seat at Wu.

sentences.zh: 漢順帝永建四年，分會稽為吳郡，會稽移治山陰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongjian under Emperor Shun of Han, Kuaiji was divided to form Wu Commandery, and Kuaiji moved its seat to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongjian (129), Kuaiji was split to form Wu Commandery, and the seat of Kuaiji was moved to Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 領縣十，戶五萬二千二百二十八，口三十四萬八千一十四。

translations.literal: It governed ten counties; households 52,228; persons 348,014.
translations.idiomatic: It governed ten counties, with 52,228 registered households and a population of 348,014.

sentences.zh: 去京都水一千三百五十五，陸同。

translations.literal: From the capital: 1,355 li by water; the same by land.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 1,355 li by water, the same by land.

sentences.zh: 山陰令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shanyin: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Shanyin: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 永興令，漢舊餘暨縣，吳更名。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yongxing: the old Han county of Yuji, renamed under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yongxing: the Han county of Yuji, renamed under Wu.

sentences.zh: 上虞令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shangyu: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Shangyu: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 余姚令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yuyao: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yuyao: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 剡令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shan: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Shan: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 諸暨令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Zhuji: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Zhuji: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 始甯令，何承天志，漢末分上虞立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shining: in He Chengtian's Gazetteer, established at the end of Han by division from Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Shining: according to He Chengtian's gazetteer, established late in Han by splitting off from Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 賀《續會稽記》雲：「順帝永建四年，分上虞南鄉立。

translations.literal: Hei's Continuation of the Kuaiji Record says: "In the fourth year of Yongjian under Emperor Shun, it was established by dividing the southern district of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Hei's Continuation of the Kuaiji Record states: "In the fourth year of Yongjian under Emperor Shun, it was established from the southern district of Shangyu."

sentences.zh: 」《續漢志》無。

translations.literal: " The Continuation of the Han Treatise does not have it.
translations.idiomatic: The Continuation of the Han Treatise does not mention it.

sentences.zh: 《晉太康三年地志》有。

translations.literal: The Jin Gazetteer of the Land of the third year of Taikang has it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Gazetteer of the Land for the third year of Taikang (282) does.

sentences.zh: 句章令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Juzhang: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Juzhang: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 鄮令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Mao: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Mao: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 鄞令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yin: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yin: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 吳郡太守，分會稽立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery: established by division from Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery: established by splitting off from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明七年，度屬南徐。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, it was transferred to belong to Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daming (463), it was transferred to Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 八年，復舊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year it reverted to the former status.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (464) it reverted to its former jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 領縣十二，戶五萬四百八十八，口四十二萬四千八百一十二。

translations.literal: It governed twelve counties; households 50,488; persons 424,812.
translations.idiomatic: It governed twelve counties, with 50,488 registered households and a population of 424,812.

sentences.zh: 去京都水六百七十，陸五百二十。

translations.literal: From the capital: 670 li by water, 520 li by land.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 670 li by water, 520 li by land.

sentences.zh: 吳令，漢舊縣。

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Lou: a county dating from the Han.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Jiaxing: this place was originally called Changshui and was renamed Youquan under Qin.

translations.idiomatic: Because Sun Hao's father's name was He, it was renamed again as Jiaxing.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yanguan: a county dating from the Han.

translations.literal: The Wu Record says: "Yanguan originally belonged to Jiaxing; Wu established it as the seat of the Haichang Commandant, and afterward it was changed to a county.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Record claims: "Yanguan originally belonged to Jiaxing; Wu made it the seat of the Haichang commandant, and it was later converted to a county."

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Qiantang: a county dating from the Han.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Fuyang: a county dating from the Han.

translations.idiomatic: Because Empress Dowager Zheng of Emperor Jianwen tabooed the character chun, Emperor Xiaowu renamed it Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 新城令，浙江西南名為桐溪，吳立為新城縣，後並桐廬。

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Xincheng: the region southwest of the Zhe River was called Tongxi; Wu established Xincheng County here, which was later merged with Tonglu.

translations.literal: The Jin Taikang Gazetteer of the Land does not have it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Taikang Gazetteer of the Land does not mention it.

translations.idiomatic: It may have been established late in the Taikang era and soon abolished again.

translations.idiomatic: It was re-established in the ninth year of Xianhe (334).

translations.literal: Magistrate of Jiande: established under Wu by division from Fuchun.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Jiande: established under Wu by splitting off from Fuchun.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Tonglu: established under Wu by splitting off from Fuchun.

translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Wuxing: established in the first year of Baoding (266) by splitting off from Wu and Danyang.

translations.idiomatic: It governed ten counties, with 49,609 registered households and a population of 316,173.

translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 950 li by water, 570 li by land.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Wucheng: an old Han county, formerly belonging to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Wucheng: a Han-era county formerly under Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 長城令，晉武帝太康三年，分烏程立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Changcheng: in the third year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, established by division from Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Changcheng: established in the third year of Taikang (282) by splitting off from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 原鄉令，漢靈帝中平二年，分故鄣立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yuanxiang: in the second year of Zhongping under Emperor Ling of Han, established by division from Guzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yuanxiang: established in the second year of Zhongping (185) by splitting off from Guzhang.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Anji: established in the second year of Zhongping (185) by splitting off from Guzhang.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yuhang: a Han-era county formerly under Wu Commandery.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yuqian: an old Han county, formerly belonging to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yuqian: a Han-era county formerly under Danyang.

sentences.zh: 淮南太守，秦立為九江郡，兼得廬江豫章。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Huainan: established under Qin as Jiujiang Commandery, also obtaining Lujiang and Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Huainan: established under Qin as Jiujiang Commandery, which also encompassed Lujiang and Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝四年，更名淮南國，分立豫章郡，文帝又分為廬江郡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Emperor Gaodi of Han it was renamed the Huainan State; Yuzhang Commandery was separately established; under Emperor Wen it was again divided to form Lujiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Gaodi (203 BCE) it was renamed the Huainan state; Yuzhang was split off, and under Emperor Wen Lujiang Commandery was created.

sentences.zh: 武帝元狩元年，複為九江郡，治壽春縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu it was again made Jiujiang Commandery, seat at Shouchun County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanshou (122 BCE) it was again made Jiujiang Commandery, with its seat at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 後漢徙治陰陵縣。

translations.literal: Under Later Han the seat was moved to Yinling County.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han the seat was moved to Yinling County.

sentences.zh: 魏複曰淮南，徙治壽春。

translations.literal: Under Wei it was again called Huainan, and the seat was moved to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei it was again called Huainan and the seat returned to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年，複立曆陽別見、當塗、逡道諸縣，二年，複立鐘離縣別見，並二漢舊縣也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, Liyang (see elsewhere), Dangtu, and Xundao counties were re-established; in the second year, Zhongli County (see elsewhere) was re-established—all old counties of the two Han dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taikang (280), Liyang (see elsewhere), Dangtu, and Xundao were re-established; in the second year Zhongli (see elsewhere) was as well—all counties dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 三國時，江淮為戰爭之地，其間不居者各數百里，此諸縣並在江北淮南，虛其地，無複民戶。

translations.literal: During the Three Kingdoms period the Yangzi and Huai were battlegrounds; between them uninhabited zones extended for several hundred li each. These counties were all north of the Yangzi on the Huainan side; their territory was left empty and there were no households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Three Kingdoms the Yangzi-Huai region was a war zone, with uninhabited belts hundreds of li wide. These counties lay north of the Yangzi on the Huainan side; their lands stood empty and their populations had vanished.

sentences.zh: 吳平，民各還本，故複立焉。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified the people each returned to their homes, and they were therefore re-established.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was conquered, the people returned home and the counties were re-established.

sentences.zh: 其後中原亂，胡寇屢南侵，淮南民多南度。

translations.literal: Afterward the Central Plains fell into disorder and northern barbarians repeatedly invaded south; many Huainan people crossed south.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the north fell into chaos and invaders pushed south repeatedly, many Huainan people fled south.

sentences.zh: 成帝初，蘇峻、祖約為亂于江淮，胡寇又大至，民南度江者轉多，乃於江南僑立淮南郡及諸縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Cheng, Su Jun and Zu Yue raised rebellion in the Yangzi-Huai region, and northern invaders came in great force; those who crossed south over the Yangzi grew ever more numerous, and a frontier Huainan Commandery and its counties were established south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Cheng's reign, Su Jun and Zu Yue rebelled along the Yangzi and Huai, and northern invaders swept in again. As ever more refugees crossed the Yangzi, a frontier Huainan Commandery and its counties were set up south of the river.

sentences.zh: 晉末，遂割丹陽之於湖縣為淮南境。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin, the Yuhu County of Danyang was carved off to form Huainan's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jin, Yuhu County in Danyang was carved off to form Huainan's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武大明六年，以淮南郡並宣城，宣城郡徙治於湖。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Huainan Commandery was merged into Xuancheng, and Xuancheng Commandery moved its seat to Yuhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daming (462), Huainan was merged into Xuancheng, and Xuancheng moved its seat to Yuhu.

sentences.zh: 八年，複立淮南郡，屬南豫州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Huainan Commandery was re-established and placed under Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (464) Huainan was re-established under Southern Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始三年，還屬揚州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi under Emperor Ming it was returned to Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taishi (467) it was returned to Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 領縣六，戶五千三百六十二，口二萬五千八百四十。

translations.idiomatic: It governed six counties, with 5,362 registered households and a population of 25,840.

sentences.zh: 去京都水一百七十，陸一百四十。

translations.literal: From the capital: 170 li by water, 140 li by land.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 170 li by water, 140 li by land.

sentences.zh: 于湖令，晉武帝太康二年，分丹楊縣立，本吳督農校尉治。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yuhu: in the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, established by division from Danyang County; originally the seat of the Wu Director of Agricultural Colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yuhu: established in the second year of Taikang (281) by splitting off from Danyang; originally the seat of Wu's Director of Agricultural Colonies.

sentences.zh: 當塗令，晉成帝世，與逡道俱立為僑縣，晉末分於湖為境。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Dangtu: in the era of Emperor Cheng of Jin, together with Xundao it was established as a frontier county; at the end of Jin territory was divided from Yuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Dangtu: under Emperor Cheng of Jin, established with Xundao as a frontier county; late in Jin its territory was carved from Yuhu.

sentences.zh: 繁昌令，漢舊名，本屬潁川。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Fanchang: an old Han name, originally belonging to Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Fanchang: a Han-era name originally belonging to Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 魏分潁川為襄城，又屬焉。

translations.literal: Under Wei Yingchuan was divided to form Xiangcheng, and it then belonged there.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, Yingchuan was split to form Xiangcheng, to which it then belonged.

sentences.zh: 晉亂，省襄城郡，以此縣屬淮南，割於湖為境。

translations.literal: During the Jin disorders Xiangcheng Commandery was abolished, and this county was placed under Huainan, with territory carved from Yuhu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin disorders Xiangcheng Commandery was abolished and the county placed under Huainan, with territory carved from Yuhu.

sentences.zh: 襄垣令，其地本蕪湖。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Xiangyuan: its territory was originally Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Xiangyuan: its territory was originally Wuhu.

translations.idiomatic: Wuhu County: a county dating from the Han.

translations.idiomatic: By the end of Jin, Xiangyuan County was established under Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 上党民南過江，立僑郡縣，寄治蕪湖，後省上黨郡為縣，屬淮南。

translations.literal: Shangdang people crossed south over the Yangzi and established frontier commanderies and counties, administering from Wuhu; later Shangdang Commandery was reduced to a county and placed under Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from Shangdang crossed the Yangzi and set up frontier commanderies and counties administered from Wuhu; later Shangdang Commandery was reduced to a county under Huainan.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉九年，省上黨縣並襄垣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Shangdang County was abolished and merged into Xiangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia (432) Shangdang County was abolished and merged into Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 定陵令，漢舊名，本屬襄城，後割蕪湖為境。

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Dingling: a Han-era name originally belonging to Xiangcheng; later its territory was carved from Wuhu.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Lincheng: established under Wu.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Guangyang: the old Han county was called Lingyang; Ziming attained immortality on a mountain in this county, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Guangyang: the Han county was called Lingyang, renamed for Ziming, who attained immortality on a mountain here.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shicheng: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Shicheng: a county dating from the Han.

translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Dongyang: originally the Western Commandant of Kuaiji; established in the first year of Baoding (266) under Sun Hao.

sentences.zh: 領縣九，戶一萬六千二十二，口一十萬七千九百六十五。

translations.literal: It governed nine counties; households 16,022; persons 107,965.
translations.idiomatic: It governed nine counties, with 16,022 registered households and a population of 107,965.

translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 1,700 li by water, the same by land.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Changshan: established in the second year of Chuping (191) by splitting off from Wushang.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Wuning: established in the second year of Xingping (195) by the Sun clan from Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 豐安令，漢獻帝興平二年，孫氏分諸暨立。

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Feng'an: established in the second year of Xingping (195) by the Sun clan from Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 定陽令，漢獻帝建安二十三年，孫氏分信安立。

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Dingyang: established in the twenty-third year of Jian'an (218) by the Sun clan from Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 臨海太守，本會稽東部都尉。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Linhai: originally the Eastern Commandant of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Linhai: originally the Eastern Commandant of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 前漢都尉治鄞，後漢分會稽為吳郡，疑是都尉徙治章安也。

translations.literal: Under Former Han the commandant's seat was at Yin; under Later Han Kuaiji was divided to form Wu Commandery—it is suspected the commandant then moved his seat to Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Under Former Han the commandant was at Yin; after Later Han split Kuaiji to form Wu Commandery, the commandant likely moved to Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 孫亮太平二年立。

translations.literal: Established in the second year of Taiping under Sun Liang.

translations.idiomatic: It governed five counties, with 3,961 registered households and a population of 24,226.

translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 2,019 li by water, the same by land.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Linhai: established under Wu by division from Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 甯海令，何志，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Ninghai: in He's Gazetteer, an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Ninghai: in He's Gazetteer, a Han-era county.

sentences.zh: 按《二漢志》、《晉太康地志》無。

translations.literal: According to the Treatises of the Two Han and the Jin Taikang Gazetteer of the Land, it is not listed.
translations.idiomatic: Neither the Treatises of the Two Han nor the Jin Taikang Gazetteer of the Land mentions it.

sentences.zh: 樂安令，晉康帝分始豐立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Le'an: in the era of Emperor Kang of Jin, established by division from Shifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Le'an: established under Emperor Kang of Jin by splitting off from Shifeng.

sentences.zh: 永寧令，漢順帝永建四年，分章安東甌鄉立，或雲順帝永和三年立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yongning: in the fourth year of Yongjian under Emperor Shun of Han, established by division from the Dong'ou Township of Zhang'an—or it is said to have been established in the third year of Yonghe under Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yongning: established in the fourth year of Yongjian (129) from the Dong'ou township of Zhang'an—or possibly in the third year of Yonghe (138).

sentences.zh: 松陽令，吳立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Songyang: established under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Songyang: established under Wu.

sentences.zh: 樂成令，晉孝武甯康三年，分永寧立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yuecheng: in the third year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, established by division from Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yuecheng: established in the third year of Ningkang (375) by splitting off from Yongning.

sentences.zh: 橫陽令，晉武帝太康四年，以橫藇船屯為始陽，仍複更名。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Hengyang: in the fourth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, the Hengao ship station was made Shiyang, then renamed again.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Hengyang: in the fourth year of Taikang (283), the Hengao ship station became Shiyang and was soon renamed again.

sentences.zh: 始新令，孫權分歙立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shixin: established by Sun Quan through division from She.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Shixin: established by Sun Quan by splitting off from She.

sentences.zh: 歙令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of She: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of She: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 黟令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yi: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yi: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 南徐州刺史，晉永嘉大亂，幽、冀、青、並、兗州及徐州之淮北流民，相率過淮，亦有過江在晉陵郡界者。

translations.literal: Inspector of Southern Xu Province: during the great disorders at the Yongjia era, refugees from You, Ji, Qing, Bing, Yan, and the north of Xu Province in the region north of the Huai crossed the Huai in succession; some also crossed the Yangzi and settled within Jingling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Southern Xu Province: during the great upheaval of the Yongjia era (307–313), refugees from You, Ji, Qing, Bing, Yan, and northern Xu north of the Huai fled across the Huai in waves; some also crossed the Yangzi into Jingling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝鹹和四年，司空郗鑒又徙流民之在淮南者于晉陵諸縣，其徙過江南及留在江北者，並立僑郡縣以司牧之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng, Minister of Works Xi Jian again moved refugees from Huainan into the counties of Jingling; those who had crossed south of the Yangzi or remained north of it were all given frontier commanderies and counties for administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianhe (329), Minister of Works Xi Jian relocated Huainan refugees into Jingling's counties; those south of the Yangzi or still north of it were given frontier commanderies and counties to govern them.

sentences.zh: 徐、兗二州或治江北，江北又僑立幽、冀、青、並四州。

translations.literal: Xu and Yan provinces were sometimes administered north of the Yangzi; north of the Yangzi frontier You, Ji, Qing, and Bing provinces were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Yan were sometimes administered north of the Yangzi, where frontier You, Ji, Qing, and Bing were also established.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙七年，始分淮北為北徐，淮南猶為徐州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yixi under Emperor An, the north of the Huai was first divided off as Northern Xu, while Huainan remained Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yixi (411), the north of the Huai was first made Northern Xu, while Huainan remained Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 後又以幽、冀合徐，青、併合兗。

translations.literal: Later You and Ji were merged into Xu, and Qing was merged into Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Later You and Ji were merged into Xu, and Qing into Yan.

sentences.zh: 武帝永初二年，加徐州曰南徐，而淮北但曰徐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu under Emperor Wu, Xu Province was prefixed as Southern Xu, while the north of the Huai was simply called Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu (421), Xu was prefixed as Southern Xu, while the north of the Huai was simply Xu.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉八年，更以江北為南兗州，江南為南徐州，治京口，割揚州之晉陵、兗州之九郡僑在江南者屬焉，故南徐州備有徐、兗、幽、冀、青、並、揚七州郡邑。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, the north of the Yangzi was made Southern Yan Province and the south Southern Xu Province, seat at Jingkou; Jingling of Yang and nine commanderies of Yan established south of the Yangzi were placed under it. Thus Southern Xu had the commanderies and settlements of Xu, Yan, You, Ji, Qing, Bing, and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia (431), the north of the Yangzi became Southern Yan and the south Southern Xu, seated at Jingkou; Jingling in Yang and nine Yan commanderies south of the Yangzi were placed under it, so Southern Xu encompassed jurisdictions of Xu, Yan, You, Ji, Qing, Bing, and Yang.

sentences.zh: 《永初二年郡國志》又有南沛、南下邳、廣平、廣陵、盱眙、鐘離、海陵、山陽八郡。

translations.literal: The Yongchu second-year Commanderies and States Gazetteer also lists eight commanderies: Southern Pei, Southern Xiapi, Guangping, Guangling, Xuyi, Zhongli, Hailing, and Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu second-year Commanderies and States Gazetteer also lists Southern Pei, Southern Xiapi, Guangping, Guangling, Xuyi, Zhongli, Hailing, and Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 南沛、廣陵、海陵、山陽、盱眙、鐘離割屬南兗，南下邳並南彭城，廣平並南泰山。

translations.literal: Southern Pei, Guangling, Hailing, Shanyang, Xuyi, and Zhongli were cut off to belong to Southern Yan; Southern Xiapi was merged into Southern Pengcheng, and Guangping into Southern Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Pei, Guangling, Hailing, Shanyang, Xuyi, and Zhongli were transferred to Southern Yan; Southern Xiapi was merged into Southern Pengcheng and Guangping into Southern Taishan.

sentences.zh: 今領郡十七，縣六十三，戶七萬二千四百七十二，口四十二萬六百四十。

translations.literal: Now it governs seventeen commanderies and sixty-three counties; households 72,472; persons 420,640.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs seventeen commanderies and sixty-three counties, with 72,472 registered households and a population of 420,640.

sentences.zh: 去京都水二百四十，陸二百。

translations.literal: From the capital: 240 li by water, 200 li by land.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 240 li by water, 200 li by land.

sentences.zh: 南東海太守東海郡別見，晉元帝初，割吳郡海虞縣之北境為東海郡，立郯、朐、利城三縣，而祝其、襄賁等縣寄治曲阿。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Southern Donghai: Donghai Commandery (see elsewhere). At the beginning of Emperor Yuan of Jin, the northern border of Haiyu County in Wu Commandery was carved off to form Donghai Commandery, establishing Tan, Ju, and Licheng counties, while Zhugai, Xiangben, and other counties were administered by attachment at Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Donghai: Donghai Commandery (see elsewhere). Early under Emperor Yuan of Jin, the northern part of Haiyu in Wu was carved off as Donghai Commandery, with Tan, Ju, and Licheng established while Zhugai and Xiangben were administered from Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和中，郡移出京口，郯等三縣亦寄治於京。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mu in the Yonghe era the commandery seat moved out of Jingkou, and Tan and the other three counties were also administered from the capital by attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu in the Yonghe era the seat moved out of Jingkou, and Tan and the other three were administered from the capital.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉八年立南徐，以東海為治下郡，以丹徒屬焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia Southern Xu was established; Donghai became the seat commandery below it, and Dantu was placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia (431) Southern Xu was established; Donghai became its metropolitan commandery and Dantu was placed under it.

sentences.zh: 郯、利城並為實土。

translations.literal: Tan and Licheng both became actual territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tan and Licheng both became territories with actual jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 《永初郡國》有襄賁別見、祝其、厚丘並漢舊名、西隰何江左立四縣，文帝元嘉十二年，省厚丘並襄賁。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States has Xiangben (see elsewhere), Zhugai, Houqiu—all old Han names—and Xixi, established south of the Yangzi; in the twelfth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Houqiu was abolished and merged into Xiangben.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu Commanderies and States lists Xiangben (see elsewhere), Zhugai, Houqiu (all Han-era names), and Xixi, established south of the Yangzi; in the twelfth year of Yuanjia (435) Houqiu was abolished and merged into Xiangben.

sentences.zh: 何、徐無厚丘，餘與《永初郡國》同。

translations.literal: He and Xu have no Houqiu; the rest matches the Yongchu Commanderies and States.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xu omit Houqiu; the rest matches the Yongchu gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 其襄賁、祝其、西隰，是徐志後所省也。

translations.literal: Xiangben, Zhugai, and Xixi were abolished later in Xu's gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangben, Zhugai, and Xixi were abolished later in Xu's gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 領縣六，戶五千三百四十二，口三萬三千六百五十八。

translations.literal: It governed six counties; households 5,342; persons 33,658.
translations.idiomatic: It governed six counties, with 5,342 registered households and a population of 33,658.

sentences.zh: 郯令，漢舊名。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Tan: an old Han name.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Tan: a Han-era name.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉八年，分丹徒之峴西為境。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, the Xianxi district of Dantu was carved off as its territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia (431) the Xianxi district of Dantu was carved off as its territory.

sentences.zh: 丹徒令，本屬晉陵，古名硃方，後名谷陽，秦改曰丹徒。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Dantu: originally belonged to Jingling; ancient name Zhufang, later name Guyang; under Qin changed to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Dantu: originally under Jingling; ancient name Zhufang, later Guyang, renamed Dantu under Qin.

sentences.zh: 孫權嘉禾三年，改曰武進。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe under Sun Quan it was changed to Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiahe (234) Sun Quan renamed it Wujin.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康三年，複曰丹徒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin it was again called Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taikang (282) it was again called Dantu.

sentences.zh: 武進令，晉武帝太康二年，分丹徒、曲阿立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Wujin: in the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, established by division from Dantu and Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Wujin: established in the second year of Taikang (281) by splitting off from Dantu and Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 毗陵令，宋孝武大明末，度屬此。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Piling: at the end of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, transferred to belong here.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Piling: at the end of Daming transferred here.

sentences.zh: 朐令，漢舊名。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Ju: an old Han name.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Ju: a Han-era name.

sentences.zh: 晉江左僑立。

translations.literal: Established as a frontier county south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Established as a frontier county south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武世，分郯西界為土。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Tan's western border was carved off as territory.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Tan's western border was carved off as actual territory.

sentences.zh: 利城令，漢舊名。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Licheng: an old Han name.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Licheng: a Han-era name.

sentences.zh: 晉江左僑立。

translations.literal: Under Jin, established as a frontier county south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Established as a frontier county south of the Yangzi under Jin.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝世，與郡俱為實土。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Wen of Song, together with the commandery it became actual territory.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Song, it and the commandery both became territories with actual jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 臨沂令，漢舊名。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Linyi: an old Han name.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Linyi: a Han-era name.

translations.literal: Under Former Han it belonged to Donghai; under Later Han and Jin it belonged to Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Under Former Han it belonged to Donghai; under Later Han and Jin it belonged to Langya.

sentences.zh: 晉陵太守，吳時分吳郡無錫以西為毗陵典農校尉。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Jinling: in Wu times the region west of Wuxi in Wu Commandery was separated off as the Piling Agricultural Colony Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Jinling: in Wu times the region west of Wuxi in Wu was separated off as the Piling Agricultural Colony Commandant.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康二年，省校尉，立以為毗陵郡，治丹徒，後複還毗陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, the commandant was abolished and it was established as Piling Commandery, seat at Dantu; later the seat returned to Piling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taikang (281) the commandant was abolished and Piling Commandery was established, with its seat at Dantu; later the seat returned to Piling.

sentences.zh: 東海王越世子名毗，而東海國故食毗陵。

translations.literal: The heir apparent of Prince of Donghai Sima Yue was named Pi, and the Donghai state originally drew its fief income from Piling.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent of Prince of Donghai Sima Yue was named Pi, and the Donghai fief had originally drawn its income from Piling.

sentences.zh: 永嘉五年，帝改為晉陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongjia, the emperor changed it to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongjia (311) the emperor renamed it Jinling.

sentences.zh: 始自毗陵徙治丹徒。

translations.literal: At first the seat was moved from Piling to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: At first the seat was moved from Piling to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 太興初，郡及丹徒縣悉治京口，郗鑒複徙還丹徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, the commandery and Dantu County were both administered at Jingkou; Chi Jian again moved the seat back to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taixing era, the commandery and Dantu County were both administered at Jingkou; Chi Jian later moved the seat back to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙九年，複還晉陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi under Emperor An, the seat returned again to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yixi (413) the seat returned to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 本屬揚州，文帝元嘉八年，度屬南徐。

translations.literal: Originally it belonged to Yang Province; in the eighth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, it was transferred to belong to Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Originally under Yang Province; in the eighth year of Yuanjia (431) it was transferred to Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 領縣六，戶一萬五千三百八十二，口八萬一百一十三。

translations.idiomatic: It governed six counties, with 15,382 registered households and a population of 80,113.

translations.literal: From the provincial seat: 175 li by water; the same by land;
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the provincial seat: 175 li by water, the same by land;

sentences.zh: 去京都水四百，陸同。

translations.literal: From the capital: 400 li by water; the same by land.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 400 li by water, the same by land.

sentences.zh: 晉陵令，本名延陵，漢改曰毗陵，後與郡俱改。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Jinling: originally named Yanling; under Han changed to Piling; later changed together with the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Jinling: originally Yanling; renamed Piling under Han, and later renamed again together with the commandery.

sentences.zh: 延陵令，晉武帝太康二年，分曲阿之延陵鄉立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yanling: in the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, established by division from Yanling township of Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yanling: established in the second year of Taikang (281) by splitting off Yanling township from Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 南沙令，本吳縣司鹽都尉署。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Nansha: originally the Salt Administration Commandant's office of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Nansha: originally the Salt Administration Commandant's office of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 吳時名沙中。

translations.literal: In Wu times it was called Shazhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu times it was called Shazhong.

sentences.zh: 吳平後，立暨陽縣割屬之。

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified, Jiyang County was established and cut off to belong to it.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, Jiyang County was established and placed under it.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康七年，罷鹽署，立以為南沙縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, the salt office was abolished and it was established as Nansha County.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiankang (341) the salt office was abolished and Nansha County was established.

sentences.zh: 曲阿令，本名雲陽，秦始皇改曰曲阿。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Qu'a: originally named Yunyang; the First Emperor of Qin changed it to Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Qu'a: originally Yunyang; the First Emperor of Qin renamed it Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 吳嘉禾三年，複曰雲陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe under Wu it was again called Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiahe (238) it was again called Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康二年，複曰曲阿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin it was again called Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taikang (281) it was again called Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 暨陽令，晉武帝太康二年，分無錫、毗陵立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Jiyang: in the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, established by division from Wuxi and Piling.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Jiyang: established in the second year of Taikang (281) by splitting off from Wuxi and Piling.

sentences.zh: 陽羨令，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yangxian: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yangxian: a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 臨津令，故屬陽羨，立郡分立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Linjin: formerly belonged to Yangxian; separated when the commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Linjin: formerly part of Yangxian, separated when the commandery was established.

sentences.zh: 義鄉令，故屬長城、陽羨，立郡分立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yixiang: formerly belonged to Changcheng and Yangxian; separated when the commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yixiang: formerly part of Changcheng and Yangxian, separated when the commandery was established.

sentences.zh: 國山令，故屬陽羨，立郡分立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Guoshan: formerly belonged to Yangxian; separated when the commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Guoshan: formerly part of Yangxian, separated when the commandery was established.

sentences.zh: 綏安令，武帝永初三年，分宣城之廣德、吳興之故鄣、長城及陽羨、義鄉五縣立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Suian: in the third year of Yongchu under Emperor Wu, established by division from Guangde of Xuancheng, Guzhang of Wuxing, Changcheng, Yangxian, and Yixiang—five counties.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Suian: established in the third year of Yongchu (422) by splitting off Guangde of Xuancheng, Guzhang of Wuxing, Changcheng, Yangxian, and Yixiang.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Changle: originally Changle Commandery (see elsewhere), later merged and reduced to a county.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Xu: under Former Han it belonged to Linhuai, under Later Han to Xiapi, and the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Linhuai.

translations.literal: During Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Southern Pei was divided into Northern Pei, belonging to Southern Yan, while Southern Pei still belonged to Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia, Southern Pei was divided into Northern Pei under Southern Yan, while Southern Pei remained under Southern Xu.

translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming (460) both commanderies were merged into Southern Pengcheng.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Jiao: under Former Han it belonged to Liang; under Later Han and Jin it belonged to Pei.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Northern Ling: originally belonged to Southern Xiapi; absent in the two Han dynasties; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Northern Ling: originally under Southern Xiapi; it did not exist in either Han dynasty, and the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 本名淩，而廣陵郡舊有淩縣，晉武帝太康二年，以下邳之淩縣非舊土而同名，改為北淩。

translations.literal: Originally named Ling, but Guangling Commandery formerly had a Ling County; in the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, because Xiapi's Ling County was not old territory yet shared the name, it was changed to Northern Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Ling, but Guangling had long had a Ling County; in the second year of Taikang (281), because Xiapi's Ling County was not on its original territory yet shared the name, it was renamed Northern Ling.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Gaomi (see elsewhere): south of the Yangzi a Gaomi state was established, later becoming Southern Gaomi Commandery.

translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia (441) it was reduced to Gaomi County and placed under this commandery.

sentences.zh: 南濟陰太守，二漢、晉屬兗州，前漢初屬梁國，景帝中六年，別為濟陰國，宣帝甘露二年，更名定陶國，後還曰濟陰。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Southern Jiyin: under the two Han dynasties and Jin it belonged to Yan Province; under Former Han it initially belonged to Liang State; in the sixth year of the middle period under Emperor Jing it was separately made Jiyin State; in the second year of Ganlu under Emperor Xuan it was renamed Dingtao State, and later restored to Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Jiyin: under the two Han dynasties and Jin it belonged to Yan Province; under Former Han it initially belonged to Liang; in the sixth year of Emperor Jing's middle reign it was separated as Jiyin; in the second year of Ganlu (52 BCE) it was renamed Dingtao, and later restored to Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 南濮陽太守，本東郡，屬兗州。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Southern Puyang: originally Dong Commandery, belonging to Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Puyang: originally Dong Commandery, under Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧二年，以封子允，以東不可為國名，東郡有濮陽縣，故曰濮陽國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, to enfeoff his son Yun: since "Dong" could not serve as a principality name, and Dong Commandery had Puyang County, it was therefore called the Principality of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianning (276), to enfeoff his son Yun, "Dong" could not serve as a principality name; because Dong Commandery contained Puyang County, the seat was styled the Principality of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 濮陽，漢舊名也，允改封淮南，還曰東郡。

translations.literal: Puyang was an old Han name; when Yun was transferred to Huainan, it was again called Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Puyang was a Han-era name; when Yun was re-enfeoffed in Huainan, the commandery reverted to Dong.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，廢太孫臧為濮陽王，王尋廢，郡名遂不改。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Lun usurped the throne, he deposed the heir apparent Zang as Prince of Puyang; the prince was soon deposed, but the commandery name was never changed back.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Lun seized the throne, he demoted Heir Apparent Zang to Prince of Puyang; though the prince was soon removed, the commandery kept the name.

sentences.zh: 《永初郡國》又有鄄城縣。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States also has Juancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu Commanderies and States also lists Juancheng County.

sentences.zh: 二漢屬濟陰，《晉太康地志》屬濮陽也。

translations.literal: In the two Han dynasties it belonged to Jiyin; the Jin Taikang Geography places it under Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under both Han dynasties it belonged to Jiyin; the Jin Taikang Geography assigns it to Puyang.

sentences.zh: 今領縣二，戶二千二十六，口八千二百三十九。

translations.literal: Now it governs two counties; households 2,026; persons 8,239.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs two counties, with 2,026 registered households and a population of 8,239.

sentences.zh: 廩丘令，前漢及《晉太康地志》有廩丘縣，後漢無。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Linqiu: Former Han and the Jin Taikang Geography have Linqiu County; Later Han does not.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Linqiu: listed in Former Han and the Jin Taikang Geography, but absent from Later Han.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉十二年，以鄄城並廩丘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Juancheng was merged into Linqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia (435), Juancheng was merged into Linqiu.

sentences.zh: 榆次令，漢舊名，至晉屬太原。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yuci: an old Han name; by the Jin period it belonged to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yuci: a Han-era name that by the Jin belonged to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 南泰山太守泰山郡別見，《永初郡國》有廣平漢武帝征和二年，立為平幹國。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Southern Taishan: Taishan Commandery (see elsewhere). The Yongchu Commanderies and States has Guangping; in the second year of Zhenghe under Emperor Wu of Han it was established as the Pinggan Principality.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Taishan: Taishan Commandery (see elsewhere). The Yongchu gazetteer lists Guangping, established in the second year of Zhenghe (91 BCE) as the Pinggan Principality.

sentences.zh: 宣帝五鳳二年，改為廣平。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wufeng under Emperor Xuan it was changed to Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wufeng (55 BCE) it was renamed Guangping.

sentences.zh: 光武建武十三年，省並钜鹿。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jianwu under Emperor Guangwu it was abolished and merged into Ju.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jianwu (37), it was abolished and merged into Ju.

sentences.zh: 魏分钜鹿、魏郡複為廣平。

translations.literal: Under Wei, Ju and Wei Commandery were again divided to re-establish Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, territory was split from Ju and Wei Commandery to restore Guangping.

sentences.zh: 江左僑立郡，晉成帝咸康四年省，後又立。
