translations.idiomatic: Established as a refugee seat in Xu lands, with boundaries cut from surrounding territory.

sentences.zh: 領縣三，戶二千三百五，口一萬一千九百二十八。

translations.literal: It governed three counties; households 2,305; persons 11,928.
translations.idiomatic: It governed three counties, with 2,305 registered households and a population of 11,928.

sentences.zh: 睢陵令，前漢屬臨淮，後漢屬下邳。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Suiling: in Former Han belonged to Linhuai; in Later Han to Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Suiling: under Former Han it belonged to Linhuai; under Later Han to Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明元年度。

translations.literal: Abolished in the first year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in the first year of Daming (457).

sentences.zh: 定陶令，漢舊名。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Dingtao: an old Han name.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Dingtao: a Han-era name.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明五年改為長。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu it was reduced to chief-magistrate rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming (461) it was demoted to chief-magistrate rank.

sentences.zh: 頓丘令，屬頓丘，流寓割配。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Dunqiu: belonged to Dunqiu; allotted by carving from migrant territory.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Dunqiu: under Dunqiu; assigned by partitioning refugee lands.

sentences.zh: 北濟陰太守，孝武孝建元年升立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Northern Jiyin: elevated and established in the first year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Northern Jiyin: promoted to commandery rank in the first year of Xiaojian (454).

sentences.zh: 領縣三，戶九百二十七，口三千八百十。

translations.literal: It governed three counties; households 927; persons 3,810.
translations.idiomatic: It governed three counties, with 927 registered households and a population of 3,810.

sentences.zh: 城武令，前漢屬山陽，後漢、《晉太康地志》屬濟陰。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Chengwu: in Former Han belonged to Shanyang; in Later Han and the Jin Taikang Geography belonged to Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Chengwu: under Former Han it belonged to Shanyang; under Later Han and in the Jin Taikang Geography it belonged to Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 豐令，漢舊名，屬沛。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Feng: an old Han name, belonging to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Feng: a Han-era name under Pei.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明元年複立。

translations.literal: Restored in the first year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Restored in the first year of Daming (457).

sentences.zh: 離狐令，前漢屬東郡，後漢、《晉太康地志》屬濟陰。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Lihu: in Former Han belonged to Dong Commandery; in Later Han and the Jin Taikang Geography belonged to Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Lihu: under Former Han it belonged to Dong Commandery; under Later Han and in the Jin Taikang Geography it belonged to Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 鐘離太守，本屬南兗州，晉安帝分立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Zhongli: originally belonged to Southern Yan Province; separately established under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Zhongli: originally under Southern Yan Province; split off under Emperor An of Jin.

sentences.zh: 案漢九江郡、晉淮南郡有鐘離縣，即此地也。

translations.literal: Examination shows that Han Jiujiang Commandery and Jin Huainan Commandery both had Zhongli County; this is that place.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, Han Jiujiang and Jin Huainan both included Zhongli County—this is that seat.

sentences.zh: 領縣三，戶三千二百七十二，口一萬七千八百三十二。

translations.literal: It governed three counties; households 3,272; persons 17,832.
translations.idiomatic: It governed three counties, with 3,272 registered households and a population of 17,832.

sentences.zh: 去京都陸六百二十，水一千三十。

translations.literal: From the capital: 620 li by land, 1,030 li by water.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 620 li by land, 1,030 li by water.

sentences.zh: 燕縣令別見，故屬東燕。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yan County (see elsewhere); formerly belonged to Eastern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yan County (see elsewhere); formerly under Eastern Yan.

sentences.zh: 流寓因配。

translations.literal: Assigned through migrant registration.
translations.idiomatic: Allotted through refugee registration.

sentences.zh: 朝歌令，本屬河內，晉武帝分河內為汲，又屬焉。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Chaoge: originally belonged to Henei; when Emperor Wu of Jin divided Henei to form Ji, it again belonged there.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Chaoge: originally under Henei; when Emperor Wu of Jin split Henei to create Ji, it was placed under Ji.

sentences.zh: 流寓因配。

translations.literal: Assigned through migrant registration.
translations.idiomatic: Allotted through refugee registration.

sentences.zh: 樂平令，前漢曰清，屬東郡，章帝更名，《晉太康地志》無。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yueping: in Former Han called Qing, belonging to Dong Commandery; Emperor Zhang renamed it; the Jin Taikang Geography does not list it.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yueping: called Qing under Former Han in Dong Commandery; Emperor Zhang renamed it; absent from the Jin Taikang Geography.

sentences.zh: 流寓因配。

translations.literal: Assigned through migrant registration.
translations.idiomatic: Allotted through refugee registration.

sentences.zh: 馬頭太守，屬南豫州，故淮南當塗縣地，晉安帝立，因山形立名。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Matou: belonging to Southern Yu Province; on the old Huainan seat of Dangtu County; established under Emperor An of Jin and named for the mountain's shape.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Matou: under Southern Yu Province, on former Huainan Dangtu County territory; established under Emperor An of Jin and named for the local terrain.

sentences.zh: 領縣三，戶一千三百三十二，口一萬二千三百一十。

translations.literal: It governed three counties; households 1,332; persons 12,310.
translations.idiomatic: It governed three counties, with 1,332 registered households and a population of 12,310.

sentences.zh: 去京都水一千七百五十，陸六百七十。

translations.literal: From the capital: 1,750 li by water, 670 li by land.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 1,750 li by water, 670 li by land.

sentences.zh: 虞縣令，漢舊名，屬梁郡。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yu County: an old Han name, belonging to Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Yu County: a Han-era name under Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 流寓因配。

translations.literal: Assigned through migrant registration.
translations.idiomatic: Allotted through refugee registration.

sentences.zh: 零縣令，晉安帝立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Ling County: established under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Ling County: established under Emperor An of Jin.

sentences.zh: 濟陽令，故屬濟陽。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Jiyang: formerly belonged to Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Jiyang: formerly under Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 流寓因配。

translations.literal: Assigned through migrant registration.
translations.idiomatic: Allotted through refugee registration.

sentences.zh: 新昌太守，後廢帝元徽元年立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Xinchang: established in the first year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Xinchang: established in the first year of Yuanhui (473).

sentences.zh: 南兗州刺史，中原亂，北州流民多南渡，晉成帝立南兗州，寄治京口。

translations.literal: Inspector of Southern Yan Province: when the Central Plains fell into disorder, many refugees from the northern provinces fled south; Emperor Cheng of Jin established Southern Yan Province with provisional seat at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Southern Yan Province: amid turmoil in the Central Plains, refugees from the north fled south in great numbers; Emperor Cheng of Jin created Southern Yan Province, provisionally seated at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 時又立南青州及并州，武帝永初元年，省並並南兗。

translations.literal: Southern Qing Province and Bing Province were also established at the time; in the first year of Yongchu under Emperor Wu, Bing was abolished and merged into Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qing and Bing provinces were also set up at the time; in the first year of Yongchu (420), Bing was abolished and absorbed into Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉八年，始割江淮間為境，治廣陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, territory between the Jiang and Huai was first carved out as its border, with seat at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia (431), the province was first bounded by lands between the Yangzi and Huai, with its seat at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 《永初郡國》領十四郡。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States governed fourteen commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu gazetteer lists fourteen commanderies.

sentences.zh: 南高平、南平昌、南濟陰、南濮陽、南泰山、濟陽、南魯山郡，今並屬徐州。

translations.literal: Southern Gaoping, Southern Pingchang, Southern Jiyin, Southern Puyang, Southern Taishan, Jiyang, and Southern Lushan commanderies now all belong to Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Gaoping, Southern Pingchang, Southern Jiyin, Southern Puyang, Southern Taishan, Jiyang, and Southern Lushan now all fall under Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 又有東燕郡，江左分濮陽所立也，領燕縣前漢曰南燕，後漢曰燕，並屬東郡。

translations.literal: There was also Eastern Yan Commandery, established south of the Yangzi by division from Puyang; it governed Yan County—in Former Han called Southern Yan, in Later Han called Yan—both belonging to Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Eastern Yan Commandery, set up south of the Yangzi from Puyang; it governed Yan County—Southern Yan under Former Han, Yan under Later Han—both formerly under Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 《太康地志》屬濮陽。

translations.literal: The Taikang Geography places it under Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Taikang Geography assigns it to Puyang.

sentences.zh: 、白馬、平昌、考城凡四縣。

translations.literal: Baima, Pingchang, and Kaocheng—four counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Baima, Pingchang, and Kaocheng—four counties in all.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉十八年，省考城並燕。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Kaocheng was abolished and merged into Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia (441), Kaocheng was abolished and merged into Yan.

sentences.zh: 十九年，省東燕郡為東燕縣，屬南濮陽，後又省東燕郡。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Eastern Yan Commandery was abolished to form Eastern Yan County, subordinate to Southern Puyang; later Eastern Yan Commandery was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year (442), Eastern Yan Commandery was reduced to Eastern Yan County under Southern Puyang; the commandery was abolished again afterward.

sentences.zh: 南東平郡領範、蛇丘、曆城凡三縣。

translations.literal: Southern Dongping Commandery governed Fan, Sheqiu, and Licheng—three counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Dongping Commandery governed Fan, Sheqiu, and Licheng—three counties altogether.

sentences.zh: 高密郡領淳於、黔陬、營陵、夷安凡四縣。

translations.literal: Gaomi Commandery governed Chunyu, Qianzou, Yingling, and Yi'an—four counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Gaomi Commandery governed Chunyu, Qianzou, Yingling, and Yi'an—four counties altogether.

sentences.zh: 南齊郡領安西、臨菑凡二縣。

translations.literal: Southern Qi Commandery governed Anxi and Linzi—two counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qi Commandery governed Anxi and Linzi—two counties altogether.

sentences.zh: 南平原郡領平原、高唐、茌平並別見凡三縣。

translations.literal: Southern Pingyuan Commandery governed Pingyuan, Gaotang, and Chiping (all see elsewhere)—three counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Pingyuan Commandery governed Pingyuan, Gaotang, and Chiping (see elsewhere)—three counties altogether.

sentences.zh: 濟岷郡江左立，領營城、晉甯江左立凡二縣。

translations.literal: Jimin Commandery was established south of the Yangzi; it governed Yingcheng and Jinning, the latter also established south of the Yangzi—two counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Jimin Commandery was set up south of the Yangzi; it governed Yingcheng and Jinning, the latter also a Yangzi-crossing establishment—two counties altogether.

sentences.zh: 雁門郡漢舊郡領樓煩別見、陰館前漢作「觀」，後漢、晉作「館」也。

translations.literal: Yanmen Commandery, an old Han commandery, governed Loufan (see elsewhere) and Yinguan—in Former Han written with the "observe" graph, in Later Han and Jin with the "office" graph.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmen Commandery, a Han-era seat, governed Loufan (see elsewhere) and Yinguan—written with the character for "observe" under Former Han and the homophonous character for "office" under Later Han and Jin.

sentences.zh: 、廣武前漢屬太原，後漢、《晉太康地志》屬雁門也。

translations.literal: Guangwu—in Former Han belonged to Taiyuan; in Later Han and the Jin Taikang Geography belonged to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu: under Former Han it belonged to Taiyuan; under Later Han and in the Jin Taikang Geography it belonged to Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 、崞、馬邑並漢舊名凡五縣。

translations.literal: Guo, Mayi—all old Han names—five counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Guo and Mayi, all Han-era names—five counties in all.

sentences.zh: 凡七郡，二十三縣，並省屬南徐州。

translations.literal: Seven commanderies and twenty-three counties in all were abolished and placed under Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether seven commanderies and twenty-three counties were abolished and assigned to Southern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 諸僑郡縣何志又有鐘離、雁門、平原、東平、北沛五郡。

translations.literal: Among the frontier commanderies and counties, He Chengtian's Gazetteer also lists Zhongli, Yanmen, Pingyuan, Dongping, and Northern Pei—five commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's gazetteer of frontier seats also records Zhongli, Yanmen, Pingyuan, Dongping, and Northern Pei—five commanderies.

sentences.zh: 鐘離今屬徐州。

translations.literal: Zhongli now belongs to Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli now falls under Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 雁門領樓煩、陰館、廣武三縣。

translations.literal: Yanmen governed Loufan, Yinguan, and Guangwu—three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmen governed Loufan, Yinguan, and Guangwu—three counties.

sentences.zh: 平原領茌平、臨菑、營城、平原四縣。

translations.literal: Pingyuan governed Chiping, Linzi, Yingcheng, and Pingyuan—four counties.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan governed Chiping, Linzi, Yingcheng, and Pingyuan—four counties.

sentences.zh: 東平領範、朝陽、曆城三縣。

translations.literal: Dongping governed Fan, Chaoyang, and Licheng—three counties.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping governed Fan, Chaoyang, and Licheng—three counties.

sentences.zh: 北沛領符離、蕭、相、沛四縣。

translations.literal: Northern Pei governed Fuli, Xiao, Xiang, and Pei—four counties.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Pei governed Fuli, Xiao, Xiang, and Pei—four counties.

sentences.zh: 符離，漢舊縣。

translations.literal: Fuli was an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Fuli was a county dating from the Han.

sentences.zh: 餘並別見。

translations.literal: The rest are all treated elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining counties are discussed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 凡十四縣。

translations.literal: Fourteen counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen counties in all.

sentences.zh: 《起居注》，元嘉十一年，以南兗州東平之平陸並范，壽張並朝陽，平原之濟岷、晉甯並營城先是，省濟岷郡為縣。

translations.literal: The Daily Records state that in the eleventh year of Yuanjia, Pinglu of Southern Yan's Dongping was merged into Fan; Shouzhang into Chaoyang; Jimin and Jinning of Pingyuan into Yingcheng. Earlier, Jimin Commandery had been abolished to form a county.
translations.idiomatic: The Daily Records note that in the eleventh year of Yuanjia (434), Pinglu in Southern Yan's Dongping was merged into Fan; Shouzhang into Chaoyang; Jimin and Jinning in Pingyuan into Yingcheng. Jimin Commandery had already been reduced to a county.

sentences.zh: ，高唐並茌平。

translations.literal: Gaotang was merged into Chiping.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang was merged into Chiping.

sentences.zh: 按此五縣，元嘉十一年所省，則平陸、壽張疑在《永初郡國志》，而無此二縣，未詳。

translations.literal: Examining these five abolished counties of the eleventh year of Yuanjia, Pinglu and Shouzhang would seem to appear in the Yongchu Commanderies and States, yet those two counties are not listed—this is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: These five counties abolished in Yuanjia 11 suggest Pinglu and Shouzhang ought to appear in the Yongchu gazetteer, yet neither is listed—the reason is unclear.

sentences.zh: 徐志有南東平郡，領範、朝陽、曆城、樓煩、陰觀、廣武、茌平、營城、臨菑、平原十縣，則是雁門、平原並東平也。

translations.literal: The Liu Song Gazetteer has Southern Dongping Commandery governing Fan, Chaoyang, Licheng, Loufan, Yinguan, Guangwu, Chiping, Yingcheng, Linzi, and Pingyuan—ten counties—showing that Yanmen and Pingyuan were merged into Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Song gazetteer lists Southern Dongping with Fan, Chaoyang, Licheng, Loufan, Yinguan, Guangwu, Chiping, Yingcheng, Linzi, and Pingyuan—ten counties—indicating that Yanmen and Pingyuan were absorbed into Dongping.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明五年，以東平並廣陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, Dongping was merged into Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming (461), Dongping was merged into Guangling.

sentences.zh: 宋又僑立新平、北淮陽、北濟陰、北下邳、東莞五郡。

translations.literal: Under Song, five frontier commanderies were also established anew: Xinping, Northern Huaiyang, Northern Jiyin, Northern Xiapi, and Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Song also set up five new refugee commanderies: Xinping, Northern Huaiyang, Northern Jiyin, Northern Xiapi, and Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年，南兗州徙治盱眙。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, Southern Yan Province moved its seat to Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia (451), Southern Yan Province relocated its seat to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 三十年，省南兗州並南徐，其後複立，還治廣陵。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Southern Yan was abolished and merged into Southern Xu; it was later restored and returned its seat to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (453), Southern Yan was abolished and merged into Southern Xu; it was later re-established with its seat back at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 徐志領郡九，縣三十九，戶三萬一千一百一十五，口十五萬九千三百六十二。

translations.literal: The Liu Song Gazetteer governed nine commanderies and thirty-nine counties; households 31,115; persons 159,362.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Song gazetteer records nine commanderies and thirty-nine counties, with 31,115 registered households and a population of 159,362.

sentences.zh: 宋末領郡十一，縣四十四。

translations.literal: At the end of Song it governed eleven commanderies and forty-four counties.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Song it governed eleven commanderies and forty-four counties.

sentences.zh: 去京都水二百五十，陸一百八十。

translations.literal: From the capital: 250 li by water, 180 li by land.
translations.idiomatic: Distance from the capital: 250 li by water, 180 li by land.

sentences.zh: 廣陵太守，漢高六年立，屬荊國，十一年，更屬吳；

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Guangling: established in the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu of Han, belonging to Jing Principality; in the eleventh year it was transferred to Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Guangling: established in the sixth year of Emperor Gaozu of Han (201 BCE), under Jing Principality; in the eleventh year (196) it passed to Wu;

sentences.zh: 景帝四年，更名江都國；

translations.literal: in the fourth year of Emperor Jing it was renamed Jiangdu Principality;
translations.idiomatic: in the fourth year of Emperor Jing (153 BCE) it was renamed Jiangdu Principality;

sentences.zh: 武帝元狩三年，更名廣陵。

translations.literal: in the third year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu it was renamed Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: in the third year of Yuanshou (116 BCE) it was renamed Guangling.

sentences.zh: 舊屬徐州。

translations.literal: Formerly belonged to Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly under Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康三年，治淮陰故城，後又治射陽射陽別見。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, the seat was at the old city of Huaiyin; later it was also seated at Sheyang (see elsewhere).
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taikang (282), the seat was moved to old Huaiyin; it was later seated at Sheyang as well (see elsewhere).

sentences.zh: 江左治廣陵。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi, the seat was at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangzi, the seat was at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 《永初郡國》又有輿前漢屬臨淮，後漢省臨淮屬廣陵，文帝元嘉十三年並江都也。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States also has Yu—in Former Han it belonged to Linhuai; in Later Han Linhuai was abolished and it belonged to Guangling; in the thirteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen it was merged into Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu gazetteer also lists Yu: under Former Han it belonged to Linhuai; under Later Han, when Linhuai was abolished, to Guangling; in the thirteenth year of Yuanjia (436) it was merged into Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 、肥如、潞、真定、新市五縣。

translations.literal: Feiru, Lu, Zhending, and Xinshi—five counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Feiru, Lu, Zhending, and Xinshi—five counties in all.

sentences.zh: 並二漢舊名。

translations.literal: All are old names from the two Han dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: All are names dating from both Han dynasties.

sentences.zh: 肥如屬遼西，潞屬上黨，真定前漢屬真定，後漢省真定屬常山，晉亦屬常山。

translations.literal: Feiru belonged to Liaoxi; Lu belonged to Shangdang; Zhending under Former Han belonged to Zhending, under Later Han Zhending was abolished and it belonged to Changshan, and under Jin it also belonged to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Feiru belonged to Liaoxi; Lu to Shangdang; Zhending, a Former Han seat of Zhending commandery, was placed under Changshan after Later Han abolished Zhending commandery, and remained under Changshan in Jin.

sentences.zh: 新市二漢、晉屬中山。

translations.literal: Xinshi under the two Han dynasties and Jin belonged to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xinshi belonged to Zhongshan under both Han dynasties and under Jin.

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States has Dong, Chenliu, and Puyang—three commanderies—and lacks Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu gazetteer lists Dong, Chenliu, and Puyang but not Yangping.

sentences.zh: 東郡領白馬別見、涼城二漢東郡有聊城縣，《晉太康地志》無，疑此是。

translations.literal: Dong Commandery governed Baima (see elsewhere) and Liangcheng; in the two Han dynasties Dong Commandery had Liaocheng County, absent from the Jin Taikang Geography—this is suspected to be that.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Commandery governed Baima (see elsewhere) and Liangcheng; both Han dynasties placed Liaocheng in Dong Commandery, though the Jin Taikang Geography omits it—likely the same place.

sentences.zh: 、東燕別見三縣。

translations.literal: , and Dongyan (see elsewhere)—three counties.
translations.idiomatic: , and Dongyan (see elsewhere)—three counties in all.

sentences.zh: 陳留郡領酸棗漢舊縣、小黃、雍丘、白馬、襄邑、尉氏六縣。

translations.literal: Chenliu Commandery governed Suizao (Han old county), Xiaohuang, Yongqiu, Baima, Xiangyi, and Weishi—six counties.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu Commandery governed Suizao (a Han-era county), Xiaohuang, Yongqiu, Baima, Xiangyi, and Weishi—six counties.

sentences.zh: 郡縣並別見。

translations.literal: Commandery and counties all (see elsewhere).
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and its counties are all discussed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 濮陽郡領濮陽、廩丘並別見二縣。

translations.literal: Puyang Commandery governed Puyang and Linqiu (both see elsewhere)—two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Puyang Commandery governed Puyang and Linqiu (both see elsewhere)—two counties.

sentences.zh: 宋末失淮北，僑立兗州，寄治淮陰淮陰別見。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, when north of the Huai was lost, a frontier Yan Province was established, administered from Huaiyin (see elsewhere).
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Song, after territory north of the Huai was lost, a frontier Yan Province was set up with its seat attached at Huaiyin (see elsewhere).

sentences.zh: 兗州領郡六，縣三十一，戶二萬九千三百四十，口一十四萬五千五百八十一。

translations.literal: Yan Province governed six commanderies and thirty-one counties; households 29,340; persons 145,581.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Province governed six commanderies and thirty-one counties, with 29,340 registered households and a population of 145,581.

sentences.zh: 泰山太守，漢高立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Taishan: established under Emperor Gaozu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Taishan: established under Emperor Gaozu of Han.

sentences.zh: 《永初郡國》又有山茌別見、萊蕪漢舊名、太原本郡，僑立此縣三縣，而無钜平縣。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States also has Shanzhi (see elsewhere), Laiwu (old Han name), and a county from the original Taiyuan Commandery—three counties established here as frontier administration—and lacks Juping County.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu gazetteer also lists Shanzhi (see elsewhere), Laiwu (a Han-era name), and a county from original Taiyuan—all three established here as frontier counties—but not Juping.

sentences.zh: 今領縣八，戶八千一百七十七，口四萬五千五百八十一。

translations.literal: It now governs eight counties; households 8,177; persons 45,581.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs eight counties, with 8,177 registered households and a population of 45,581.

sentences.zh: 領縣五，戶四千一百五十九，口一萬七千二百九十五。

translations.literal: It governed five counties; households 4,159; persons 17,295.
translations.idiomatic: It governed five counties, with 4,159 registered households and a population of 17,295.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Xuchang: under Former Han it belonged to Dong Commandery; under Later Han and the Jin Taikang Geography it belonged to Dongping.

translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Shouzhang: in the Spring and Autumn era it was called Liang; under Former Han it was Shouliang, under Dong Commandery;

translations.literal: Guangwu changed it to Shouzhang, belonging to Dongping.

translations.idiomatic: It governed five counties, with 2,857 registered households and a population of 11,271.
